input.final_result:
Answer: Amazon (AMZN) plans to spend the most on capex in 2025, at roughly $100 billion. Alphabet (GOOG) is second at about $75 billion, and Meta (META) is third at up to $65 billion. These are the Q4 2024 earnings-call guidance figures, as of April 7, 2025.

Amazon (~$100B): Amazon CFO Brian Olsavsky said the company expects to boost capex to $100 billion in 2025, up from roughly $83 billion in 2024. This is an approximation tied to the Q4 run rate: Jassy said the $26.3B Q4 spend was "reasonably representative" of the 2025 capital investment rate, and that the vast majority is for AI for AWS.

Alphabet (~$75B): Alphabet said it expects to invest about $75 billion in capex this year.

Meta (up to $65B): Meta said it will spend as much as $65 billion on capex, including data center and computing infrastructure.

Comparison:
- Amazon vs. Alphabet: $100B - $75B = $25B more, about 33.33% above Alphabet.
- Amazon vs. Meta: $100B - $65B = $35B more, about 53.85% above Meta's top-end guidance.

Amazon's figure is the largest. Its $100B is an approximation from the run rate, while Alphabet's and Meta's are explicit guidance. Later-dated search results were excluded as they postdate April 7, 2025.
